summary: The @gyomu/ai-react package provides React-specific hooks and utilities for integrating Gyomu chat sessions into front-end applications. It acts as a bridge between the AI SDK and Gyomu-specific transport protocols, ensuring seamless message management and error handling.
responsibilities: Bridge the AI SDK chat interfaces with Gyomu communication protocols.
Manage the lifecycle and state of active chat sessions within React components.
Normalize disparate message formats between AI models and internal Gyomu structures.
Implement standardized error handling and status reporting for network and application-level exceptions.
Provide robust data extraction utilities for parsing complex UI message objects.

capabilities.name: Chat Session Management
capabilities.description: Provides React hooks to initiate, control, and observe the state of a Gyomu-powered chat session.

capabilities.name: Message Transformation
capabilities.description: Standardizes message formats by mapping AI SDK primitives to application-specific schema requirements.

capabilities.name: Transport Error Handling
capabilities.description: Standardizes the parsing and reporting of network and service errors to ensure a consistent user experience during API failures.

capabilities.name: Message Content Utilities
capabilities.description: Offers helper functions to extract readable content from complex, multi-part chat message structures.

designDecisions: Adopts a hook-based architecture to provide idiomatic React integration for complex stateful chat logic.
Decouples transport logic from UI components by utilizing specialized mapping functions for message translation.
Standardizes communication through a centralized error schema to prevent fragmented error handling across the client application.
usageGuidance: Use the 'useGyomuChat' hook as the primary entry point for implementing chat features within React components.
Leverage the provided mapping utilities when interfacing with raw AI SDK messages to ensure compatibility with Gyomu backends.
Always wrap network-sensitive fetch operations in the provided fetch wrappers to ensure consistent error parsing and exception handling.
Rely on the defined status types when building custom UI components to ensure accurate reflection of chat connection and message processing states.
